question_text: When driving outside of a built-up area, you want to overtake cyclists or pedestrians. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
comment: Outside built-up areas, the minimum distance to be maintained for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 2 metres.

question_text: Driving within a built-up area, you want to overtake a cyclist. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
comment: When overtaking, you must keep a sufficient distance to the side so as not to endanger other road users. In built-up areas, the minimum distance for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 1.5 metres.

question_text: Driving within a built-up area, you want to overtake an electric scooter. What is the minimum space to the side that you must maintain?
comment: When overtaking, you must keep a sufficient distance to the side so as not to endanger other road users. In built-up areas, the minimum distance for pedestrians, cyclists and personal transporters is 1.5 metres.

question_text: Where is overtaking prohibited?

options.text: When the traffic situation is not clear
Where oncoming traffic could be obstructed
In all one-way streets

correct_answers.text: When the traffic situation is not clear
Where oncoming traffic could be obstructed

comment: Overtaking is prohibited in the following cases: 1. in the event of an unclear traffic situation; 2. in the event of violation of traffic regulations. In one-way streets, however, there is no general rule of no overtaking. Before you start the overtaking process, look back in the mirror and over your shoulder to make sure you are not hindering or jeopardizing other road users.

question_text: What is the correct procedure for pulling out to overtake?

options.text: There is no danger to the traffic behind
Oncoming traffic is not endangered
The vehicle in front indicates right

correct_answers.text: There is no danger to the traffic behind
Oncoming traffic is not endangered

comment: For pulling out when overtaking the following rules apply: You need to convince yourself with a look in the mirror and a glance over the shoulder that your overtaking maneuver will neither jeopardize nor hinder subsequent traffic. Only then you are allowed to indicate and pull out. During the overtaking process you must take care not to hinder oncoming traffic. If the driver in front of you is flashing to the right, you should not be tempted to overtake.

question_text: What must you do to end an overtaking manoeuvre?

options.text: Move over to the right as soon as possible without inconveniencing the vehicle you have overtaken
Signal your intention to draw in clearly and in good time
Move over to the right-hand side of the roadway right in front of the vehicle you have overtaken

correct_answers.text: Move over to the right as soon as possible without inconveniencing the vehicle you have overtaken
Signal your intention to draw in clearly and in good time

comment: As an overtaking driver, you must merge right as soon as possible. However, do not go back into the lane as long as you're still too close to the driver you just overtook, as you may obstruct or even endanger him. Use the turn signal in good time before starting to pull out and merging back into the lane again.

question_text: What are the regulations governing speed when overtaking?

options.text: The speed of the overtaking vehicle must be appreciably higher
The permissible top speed must not be exceeded
The person being overtaken must not increase his speed

correct_answers.text: The speed of the overtaking vehicle must be appreciably higher
The permissible top speed must not be exceeded
The person being overtaken must not increase his speed

comment: You may only overtake a vehicle in front of you if you are significantly (at least 20 km/h) faster. Also, when overtaking: Do not exceed the maximum speed limit. The one who is being overtaken must not increase its initial speed during the maneuver.

question_text: What must you do when you are being overtaken?

options.text: If possible, drive on the far right
Not increase your speed
Increase your speed

correct_answers.text: If possible, drive on the far right
Not increase your speed

comment: Drive as far to the right as possible so as not to jeopardize the oncoming traffic and overtaking vehicle. During the entire overtaking process, you, as the one who is being overtaken, must not increase the speed, as otherwise safe overtaking would not be possible.

question_text: On which side must you overtake a tram which is travelling in the middle of the roadway (not a one-way street)?

options.text: On the right
On the left
On the left only if other vehicles are blocking the roadway on the right

correct_answers.text: On the right

comment: Trams must in general be overtaken on the right. If vehicles are parked here, you have to drive behind the tram. If the rails are too far to the right, trams may also be overtaken on the left.

question_text: When may a tram be overtaken on the left?

options.text: In one-way streets
When the rails run too far to the right
When the roadway (not a one-way street) to the right of the tram is blocked by other vehicles

correct_answers.text: In one-way streets
When the rails run too far to the right

comment: Rail vehicles such as trams may basically only be overtaken on the right. For once, you can overtake on the left when the rails are too far to the right or when the rail vehicle is traveling in a one-way street. The right-hand traffic obstructing vehicles are not a sufficient reason to overtake rail vehicles on the left.

question_text: Which vehicles may be overtaken only by maintaining a specially great lateral distance?

options.text: Bicycles
Motorcycles
Trams

correct_answers.text: Bicycles
Motorcycles

comment: When overtaking you must always keep sufficient distance to the road users next to you. This must be particularly large with motorcycle and bicycle riders. Single lane vehicles are more unstable and can sway. The lateral minimum distance to two-wheeled vehicles is 1.5 meters.

question_text: When must you signal?

options.text: Before pulling out to overtake or to pass
Before pulling in again after overtaking
When proceeding straight ahead as you leave a priority road which bends sharply

correct_answers.text: Before pulling out to overtake or to pass
Before pulling in again after overtaking

comment: Whenever you want to make a lane change or turn, you need to indicate. This also applies when following a turning priority road, but not when you leave the priority road straight ahead. Even if the direction indicator is set: always make sure that you do not endanger anyone when pulling out or going back into a lane.

question_text: Where is it forbidden to overtake?

options.text: At pedestrian crossings
At points in the road where visibility is poor
At special bus lanes

correct_answers.text: At pedestrian crossings
At points in the road where visibility is poor

comment: When overtaking, you must exclude dangerous situations for other road users. It is generally forbidden to overtake on pedestrian crossings and on roads that are difficult to observe. You might see oncoming vehicles too late. You may overtake the bus on the bus lane.

question_text: You are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a main road. How can you facilitate faster-moving vehicles in overtaking?

options.text: - onto the hard shoulder
- onto the parking area
- into a lay-by

correct_answers.text: - onto the hard shoulder
- onto the parking area
- into a lay-by

comment: To allow faster vehicles to overtake you on a country road, you can dodge on a suitable side stripe, a lay by or in a rest stop. It is also possible to slow down or even stop at a suitable location.

question_text: When overtaking, what do you have to observe regarding spacing?

options.text: Maintain an adequate space to the side, particularly between the vehicle and persons
To maintain an adequate space to the side between the vehicle and other road users
To maintain a greater side spacing towards multi-lane vehicles than towards single-lane vehicles

correct_answers.text: Maintain an adequate space to the side, particularly between the vehicle and persons
To maintain an adequate space to the side between the vehicle and other road users

comment: When overtaking, you must ensure that you have sufficient lateral distance to other road users: at least 1 meter to cars, trucks, buses, trams. For pedestrians and cyclists, the minimum distance is 1.5 meters. When we go back into lane you must not cut in on the driver you just overtook. (Check: Is he visible in the rearview mirror?)

question_text: How can you tell if a horse-drawn carriage wants to change direction?

options.text: The driver extends his arm
A traffic paddle is displayed
A flashing indicator

correct_answers.text: The driver extends his arm
A traffic paddle is displayed
A flashing indicator

comment: When a horse-drawn carriage wants to change its driving direction, it can be recognized by one of the following signs: The horse-drawn carriage indicates; the coachman beckons with his arm or with a signaling disk.

question_text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What should you do?

options.text: - as little noise as possible
- the most space to the side as possible
- a high engine speed

correct_answers.text: - as little noise as possible
- the most space to the side as possible

comment: Drive past the horses at an appropriate speed and with as much distance as possible. The animals may be frightened by sudden and loud noises such as a car horn or high engine speed, and may bolt. Therefore, avoid noise and proximity.

question_text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What should you do?

options.text: I maintain the most space to the side possible
I pay attention to the driver's hand signals
I overtake with a high engine speed

correct_answers.text: I maintain the most space to the side possible
I pay attention to the driver's hand signals

comment: If you want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a country road, you must do the following: Avoid unnecessary noise such as honking or driving at high engine speeds so as not to scare the horses. Pay attention to the hand gestures of the coachman, as he can assess the behavior of his horses. Keep a safe distance.

question_text: You are driving a slow-moving vehicle on a rural road. A line of vehicles is forming behind you. What should you do?

options.text: I allow the vehicles behind me to overtake
I come to a stop at a suitable place, if this is the only way the vehicles behind me can overtake
I switch on my hazard lights and drive as far to the right as possible

correct_answers.text: I allow the vehicles behind me to overtake
I come to a stop at a suitable place, if this is the only way the vehicles behind me can overtake

comment: A long queue behind a slow-moving vehicle leads to dangerous overtaking maneuvers. To make overtaking easier for the vehicles jamming behind you, reduce your speed. If the queue still does not disappear, you may need to stop on a side strip. This does not apply to highways! You must not use the hazard lights.

question_text: You want to overtake a horse-drawn carriage on a rural road. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I look for hand signals from the driver indicating he wants to turn off
I maintain a sufficient amount of distance when pulling in again
I maintain the smallest possible side clearance

correct_answers.text: I look for hand signals from the driver indicating he wants to turn off
I maintain a sufficient amount of distance when pulling in again

comment: When overtaking a carriage, you must pay attention to hand signals from the coachman, who may give you separate instructions. Carriages should always be overtaken at a safe distance so as not to frighten the horse.

question_text: What amount of side clearance must you maintain when overtaking pedestrians and cyclists?

options.text: - maintain a minimum side clearance of 1.5 m within a built-up area
- maintain a minimum side clearance of 2.0 m outside of a built-up area
- maintain a minimum side clearance of 1.0 m within a built-up area

correct_answers.text: - maintain a minimum side clearance of 1.5 m within a built-up area
- maintain a minimum side clearance of 2.0 m outside of a built-up area

comment: To protect cyclists and pedestrians, you must keep a distance of at least 1.5 metres to the side in built-up areas and at least 2 metres outside built-up areas.

question_text: What must you note when overtaking the cyclists in this situation?

options.text: The incline causes the cyclists to sway
I must overtake with at least 1.5 m of side clearance
I must overtake with at least 1.0 m of side clearance

correct_answers.text: The incline causes the cyclists to sway
I must overtake with at least 1.5 m of side clearance

comment:
When overtaking in built-up areas, you must maintain a distance of at least 1.5 metres to the side of the cyclist. 
Due to the commuting of cyclists, a larger minimum distance is recommended.

question_text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?

options.text: I remain behind [the cyclist]
I overtake [the cyclist] with a sufficient amount of side clearance
I have to allow [the pedestrian] to cross the road

correct_answers.text: I remain behind [the cyclist]

comment: The driving lane line is solid. Therefore, overtaking is forbidden here.
